bib.title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL)

question: Can one denoising sequence-to-sequence pretraining scheme serve both generation and comprehension tasks, and which noising functions work best?
hypothesis: A bidirectional encoder plus autoregressive decoder trained to reconstruct arbitrarily corrupted text generalizes BERT and GPT and works well across task types.
contributions: BART: denoising autoencoder pretraining of a standard seq2seq Transformer with arbitrary noising functions
Text infilling plus sentence shuffling found to be the best noising approach
State-of-the-art on several generation tasks while matching RoBERTa on GLUE and SQuAD
A fine-tuning scheme for machine translation that stacks a new source encoder on BART
Controlled ablation of other pretraining objectives within one framework

method.summary: A seq2seq Transformer (bidirectional encoder, left-to-right decoder) is pretrained to reconstruct original documents from corrupted ones. Base-size models compare noising objectives; a large model is pretrained at RoBERTa scale with text infilling and sentence permutation, then fine-tuned for classification, QA, summarization, dialogue and translation.
method.task: denoising pretraining of seq2seq model; fine-tuned for GLUE, SQuAD, summarization, dialogue, ELI5, WMT16 RO-EN

datasets.name: Pretraining corpus (same as RoBERTa)
datasets.size: 160Gb of news, books, stories, and web text

datasets.name: Books and Wikipedia (ablation)
datasets.source: inferred: from the comparison note that BERT was trained on books and Wikipedia data; the ablation data is only said to be identical across objectives

datasets.name: SQuAD 1.1/2.0
datasets.preprocessing: question and context concatenated into encoder and decoder; start/end classifiers

datasets.name: MNLI / GLUE
datasets.source: Williams et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2018
datasets.preprocessing: two sentences concatenated with appended EOS; EOS representation classified

datasets.name: XSum
datasets.preprocessing: first sentence of article removed for the qualitative WikiNews examples

datasets.name: WMT16 Romanian-English + back-translation data
datasets.source: Sennrich et al. (2016) for back-translation data

other.note: roughly 10% more parameters than equally sized BERT

models.name: Re-implemented objectives: LM, Permuted LM, Masked LM, Multitask Masked LM, Masked Seq2Seq

training.objective: cross-entropy between decoder output and original document (negative log likelihood); large model uses text infilling (30% of tokens masked, Poisson lambda=3 spans) plus sentence permutation
training.dropout: disabled for the final 10% of training steps (large model); rate otherwise not stated
training.regularisation: label smoothed cross entropy, smoothing 0.1, in generation fine-tuning

other.mt_finetuning: step 1 freezes most BART parameters, updates only the new random-init source encoder (6-layer Transformer), BART positional embeddings and the self-attention input projection of the encoder first layer; step 2 trains all parameters for a small number of iterations
other.ablation_tuning: minor changes to learning rate and layer normalisation tuned separately per objective; values not stated
other.fine_tuning_hyperparameters: not stated for any downstream task

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 5, duplicated trigrams removed
inference.max_tokens: min-len, max-len tuned on validation set (values not stated)

parameters.length_penalty: tuned on validation set for generation tasks; alpha = 1 for translation

metrics.name: Perplexity (PPL)
metrics.definition: log likelihood of the human text under the fine-tuned model

metrics.name: SQuAD EM/F1, GLUE Acc/Mcc, ConvAI2 F1
Human preference on XSum
metrics.definition: annotators choose better of two summaries

eval.protocol: Single runs reported in tables; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Human evaluation on XSum count of annotators and items not stated.

availability.weights: pre-trained models at the same locations

evidence.quote: we use a batch size of 8000, and train the model for 500000 steps

results.claim: BART beats the previous best (RoBERTa-based) on XSum by about 3.5 ROUGE points on all metrics.
results.setup: XSum, BART large fine-tuned, vs ROBERTASHARE
results.table: Table 4, row BART, column XSum R1 (baseline row ROBERTASHARE 41.45)

results.claim: BART sets state of the art on CNN/DailyMail.
results.table: Table 4, row BART, column CNN/DailyMail R1 (UniLM 43.33)

results.claim: On GLUE, large BART matches RoBERTa, so generation gains do not cost classification performance.
results.table: Table 2, row BART, column MNLI m/mm (89.9/90.1); RoBERTa 90.2/90.2
Table 3, row BART, column SQuAD 1.1 EM/F1 (88.8/94.6)

results.claim: BART improves over a strong back-translation baseline on WMT16 RO-EN with tuned BART.
results.setup: WMT16 RO-EN with back-translation data; step 2 tuned BART; fixed BART gets 36.29 (below baseline)
results.table: Table 8, row Tuned BART, column RO-EN
results.note: abstract rounds the gain to 1.1 BLEU

results.claim: Humans prefer BART to BERTSUMEXTABS on XSum but prefer the human reference to BART.
results.setup: XSum human eval; vs Reference BART preferred 33%, reference 67%
results.table: Table 5, row vs. BERTSUMEXTABS, column Prefer BART

results.claim: In the base-size ablation, text infilling variants give the most consistent results; document rotation and sentence shuffling alone perform poorly.
results.setup: BART Base w/ Text Infilling vs w/ Document Rotation (77.2); 1M steps, same data
results.table: Table 1, row BART Base w/ Text Infilling, column SQuAD 1.1 F1

results.claim: A pure language model is best on ELI5 perplexity, so BART is less effective when output is loosely constrained by input; BART still gains 1.2 ROUGE-L.
results.note: Table 1: LM PPL 21.40 vs BART w/ infilling 24.26

results.claim: BART's main qualitative limitation is hallucination of unsupported information.

limits: ELI5: a pure language model gets lower perplexity; BART is less effective when output is only loosely constrained by input
Main limitation is a tendency to hallucinate unsupported information (Sec 6)
Translation less effective without back-translation data and prone to overfitting; future work on regularisation
Fine-tuning hyperparameters, optimizer, learning rate, hardware and compute are not stated
Ablation permuted LM lacks XLNet's relative position embeddings and segment recurrence, so it is not a full replication
Does not reach human performance on XSum
Single runs with no variance reported

terms.definition: A number of text spans are sampled, with span lengths drawn from a Poisson distribution (lambda = 3). Each span is replaced with a single [MASK] token. 0-length spans correspond to the insertion of [MASK] tokens.
A document is divided into sentences based on full stops, and these sentences are shuffled in a random order.
